Blenda is a legendary heroine in Swedish folklore, best known from the tradition of Blendasägnen, which originates in the historical province of Småland in southern Sweden. According to the tale, she led the women of the Värend region and orchestrated a cunning attack on a Danish army that had invaded the defenseless lands.

The Ting Today we turn to one of the most important institutions in ancient Scandinavia, echoes of which survive to this day—þing.
The ting was not merely a parliament or a court; it was a ritual model of cosmic order, through which people, by assembling, re‑enacted the council of the gods.
Oaths, rulings, and judgments held force only because they were perceived as an echo of the heavenly ting, where the Æsir and Vanir decided the fates.
